value.body: A computer vision engineer builds software that lets machines understand images and video, for tasks such as detection, recognition, inspection and tracking. Employers include AI startups, product companies, automotive and manufacturing firms, and research labs. A typical day involves preparing image datasets, training and testing models, and making them run fast enough on real devices.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech AI & ML, CSE or ECE; M.Tech or MS for research roles

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Python, PyTorch or TensorFlow, OpenCV, GPUs

items.label: Typical tasks
items.value: Object detection, segmentation, OCR, video analytics

items.label: IndiaAI Mission outlay
items.note: Over five years; covers compute, datasets, startups and skilling

items.label: GPUs onboarded for common AI compute
items.note: Onboarded on the AI compute portal; not the same as in use

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually enter through internships or junior ML engineer roles, with projects or papers that show working vision models. A postgraduate degree helps for research-heavy teams.

value.title: At a glance
items: A specialised field with fewer openings than general software roles.
Projects and demonstrable results matter as much as degrees.
Next roles: senior CV/ML engineer, research engineer, ML lead.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
